### Proposal 1: Standardize status colors
Create a statusClasses(level) helper function (similar to the existing getThresholdClasses()) to return canonical {bg, text, border} tuples for status displays. Replace ~40 instances of inconsistent status color shades across ~15 files. Currently there are 4+ shade variations per status color (e.g., text-green-500, text-green-600, text-green-700, text-green-800 all used for "success"). Target standardization:
- Success: bg-green-50 / text-green-700 / border-green-200
- Warning: bg-amber-50 / text-amber-600 / border-amber-200
- Danger: bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200
- Info: bg-blue-50 / text-blue-700 / border-blue-200
- Neutral: bg-gray-50 / text-gray-500 / border-gray-200
Files affected include: StatusIndicator.tsx, Toast.tsx, ErrorDisplay.tsx, ErrorState.tsx, LoginForm.tsx, CommunityVelocityBands.tsx, and others.
IMPORTANT: The existing getThresholdClasses() in metricThresholds.ts handles METRIC thresholds (aging, carry cost, pace). This new helper would handle UI STATUS displays (success messages, error alerts, info banners, toast notifications). They serve different purposes and should remain separate.
### Proposal 2: Replace text-slate-* with text-ink-muted
4 instances in 3 files where text-slate-400 or text-slate-600 is used instead of the text-ink-muted design token:
- BulletBar.tsx line 36: text-slate-600 → text-ink-muted
- BulletBar.tsx line 61: text-slate-400 → text-ink-muted/60
- RadialRing.tsx line 72: text-slate-400 → text-ink-muted/60
- CommunityHealthWidget.tsx: text-slate-400 → text-ink-muted/60
### Proposal 3: Add focus rings to interactive elements missing them
Add focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-brand/20 focus-visible:outline-none to:
- EmptyState.tsx action buttons (both the <a> and <button> elements)
- Toast.tsx dismiss button
### Proposal 4: Resolve purple color usage (not in design system)
Purple (bg-purple-100 text-purple-700) is used in 3 files but is not defined in the design system:
- P3ScoreResults.tsx (10+ lines for AI/persona scoring section — uses bg-purple-50, text-purple-600/700/800/900, border-purple-200, bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-50 to-blue-50)
- EditCommunityForm.tsx (2 badge instances)
- CommunityJobLots.tsx (1 badge for "Phase" status)
Options considered:
A) Add a new --color-status-ai token for AI-related features
B) Remap purple to the existing status-info blue palette (bg-blue-50 text-blue-700)
Leaning toward B since adding an undocumented color expands the palette unnecessarily.
### Proposal 5: Extract shared Button component with variant prop
Currently 4 distinct inline button patterns used across the app:
1. Primary: bg-brand hover:bg-brand-hover text-white px-6 py-2 rounded-lg font-semibold
2. Secondary: border border-gray-300 bg-white hover:bg-gray-50 text-ink rounded-lg
3. Text/Link: text-brand hover:text-brand-hover font-medium text-xs underline
4. Icon: text-brand hover:text-brand-hover (no padding/background)
Proposal: Extract a <Button variant="primary|secondary|ghost|icon"> component to src/components/ui/Button.tsx. Every button instance would be migrated. This is the largest scope item.
### Proposal 6: Consolidate error display components
ErrorDisplay.tsx currently exports 3 components with duplicated red styling:
- ErrorDisplay (primary — icon + message + suggestion + retry)
- ErrorCard (wrapper — white card with centered icon)
- InlineError (compact — single-line bg-red-50)
Proposal: Merge into a single component with variant prop: <ErrorDisplay variant="inline|card|full">.
### Proposal 7: Deduplicate health score band colors
Health score visualization band hex values are duplicated in 2 files:
- BulletBar.tsx lines 48-50: #fee2e2, #fef9c3, #d1fae5
- PortfolioSummaryCard.tsx lines 288-290: same values
Proposal: Extract to a HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS constant in metricThresholds.ts and import from both files.
### Proposal 8: Fix LoadingSpinner / LoadingState size mismatch
Two loading components have inconsistent size mappings:
- LoadingSpinner: sm=h-4 w-4 (16px), md=h-8 w-8 (32px), lg=h-12 w-12 (48px)
- LoadingState: sm=w-6 h-6 (24px), md=w-8 h-8 (32px), lg=w-12 h-12 (48px)
The sm size differs by 8px between the two components. Proposal: Align LoadingState sm to match LoadingSpinner (16px).
### Proposal 9: Migrate CommunitiesList empty state to shared EmptyState component
CommunitiesList.tsx has a hand-built empty state (icon + message + description + CTA button) that duplicates the pattern of the shared EmptyState component from src/components/ui/EmptyState.tsx. Proposal: Replace with <EmptyState icon={...} message="..." description="..." action={{label: "...", href: "..."}} />.

1. **Correctness**: Is this the right technical approach? Are there better alternatives?

5. **Priority**: In what order should these be implemented to minimize risk and maximize value?

Please provide a structured evaluation for each proposal, then a recommended implementation order.

# Proposal-by-proposal evaluation

## 1) Standardize status colors (`statusClasses(level)`)
1. **Correctness**: Good approach; keeping it separate from `getThresholdClasses()` is the right separation of concerns.
2. **Risk**: Medium—broad touch surface (~15 files) can cause subtle visual regressions (especially borders/backgrounds) and “almost the same” states in dark-on-light contexts.
3. **Scope**: Reasonable if staged (introduce helper + migrate the highest-churn surfaces first: Toast/alerts/badges).

5. **Priority**: High value, but I’d do it **after** the smallest token/focus fixes so you’re not debugging two kinds of visual changes at once.
6. **Gotchas**: Ensure the chosen combos don’t accidentally become the *only* state cue (color-only). Also consider whether `Neutral: text-gray-500` is strong enough for small badge text under WCAG text contrast expectations. ([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum?utm_source=openai))

## 2) Replace `text-slate-*` with `text-ink-muted`
1. **Correctness**: Yes—aligns to your semantic tokens.
2. **Risk**: Low—straight class swaps.
3. **Scope**: Appropriately narrow.
4. **Conflict risk**: Low.
5. **Priority**: Very high (quick win).
6. **Gotchas**: `text-ink-muted/60` relies on Tailwind’s opacity handling; should be fine with v4 theme variables, but verify those tokens are defined as `--color-*` in the project’s `@theme`. ([tailwindcss.com](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives?utm_source=openai))

## 3) Add focus rings to elements missing them
1. **Correctness**: Directionally right (fixes real accessibility gaps).
2. **Risk**: Low-to-medium—can shift layout if you use borders instead of rings; rings/outline are typically safe.
3. **Scope**: Narrow and good.
4. **Conflict risk**: Low.
5. **Priority**: Very high (accessibility).
6. **Gotchas**: `ring-brand/20` is likely **too low-contrast** to reliably meet non-text contrast expectations for focus indicators—consider a stronger ring (and `ring-offset-2`) and prefer `focus-visible:outline-hidden` over `outline-none` to preserve forced-colors behavior. ([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html?utm_source=openai))

## 4) Resolve purple usage (out of system)
1. **Correctness**: B (remap to existing “info” palette) is the safer consistency play.
2. **Risk**: Medium—P3ScoreResults’ purple gradient is a lot of surface area; “AI” may lose a distinct visual identity.

## 5) Extract shared `<Button variant=...>`
1. **Correctness**: Technically sound, but only if you also solve semantics: `type="button"` defaults, disabled states, loading states, and link-vs-button behavior.
2. **Risk**: High—largest blast radius, most likely to introduce UX regressions (hover/focus/disabled), form submission bugs, and inconsistent icon sizing.
3. **Scope**: Too broad if “every button instance would be migrated” in one go; better as an incremental migration.
4. **Conflict risk**: High—will almost certainly touch files involved in the uncommitted DataGrid work.
5. **Priority**: Last (or split into “introduce Button + migrate 1–2 screens”).
6. **Gotchas**: If you need `<a>` and `<button>` interchangeably, use a polymorphic pattern (or `asChild`) with `forwardRef`; otherwise you’ll hit composition and ref issues. ([radix-ui.com](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/guides/composition?utm_source=openai))

2. **Risk**: Medium—API changes can ripple.

## Research notes (current as of Feb 17, 2026)
- **Tailwind v4 tokens**: variables declared in `@theme` become utilities (e.g. `--color-ink-muted` → `text-ink-muted`) and are also emitted as CSS variables; if a theme variable **references another CSS variable**, use `@theme inline` to avoid CSS variable resolution surprises. ([tailwindcss.com](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives?utm_source=openai))
- **Focus styling**: removing the UA outline requires a replacement; Tailwind’s `outline-hidden` preserves forced-colors behavior better than `outline-none`. ([tailwindcss.com](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/outline-style?utm_source=openai))
- **WCAG 2.1 contrast**: text needs **4.5:1** (or **3:1** for large text); non-text UI indicators (including authored focus indicators) need **3:1** against adjacent colors; focus must be visible for keyboard users. ([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum?utm_source=openai))
- **`:focus-visible`** is the right mechanism to avoid always-on rings for mouse users. ([developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/%3Afocus-visible?utm_source=openai))
- **Variant-based React components**: a typed “variant map” approach is fine; if you want stronger typing/composability, CVA (or tailwind-variants) is a common pattern, and `asChild`/polymorphic patterns require `forwardRef`. - **Tailwind v4 tokens**: variables declared in `@theme` become utilities (e.g. `--color-ink-muted` → `text-ink-muted`) and are also emitted as CSS variables; if a theme variable **references another CSS variable**, use `@theme inline` to avoid CSS variable resolution surprises. - **Focus styling**: removing the UA outline requires a replacement; Tailwind’s `outline-hidden` preserves forced-colors behavior better than `outline-none`. ([tailwindcss.com](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/outline-style?utm_source=openai))
- **WCAG 2.1 contrast**: text needs **4.5:1** (or **3:1** for large text); non-text UI indicators (including authored focus indicators) need **3:1** against adjacent colors; focus must be visible for keyboard users. ([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum?utm_source=openai))
- **`:focus-visible`** is the right mechanism to avoid always-on rings for mouse users. ([developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/%3Afocus-visible?utm_source=openai))
- **Variant-based React components**: a typed “variant map” approach is fine; if you want stronger typing/composability, CVA (or tailwind-variants) is a common pattern, and `asChild`/polymorphic patterns require `forwardRef`. ## Summary of Button Patterns in KineticBI Codebase

Based on my search through the component library, I've identified **4 primary button variants** with 3-4 most common patterns. Here's what I found:

### 1. **Primary/Action Button** (Most Common)
**Used for:** Main form submissions, primary actions, CTA buttons
```
bg-brand hover:bg-brand-hover text-white font-semibold px-6 py-3 rounded-lg transition-colors ease-out disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
```
**Examples:**
- AddCommunityForm.tsx line 223: "Add Community" button
- FloorPlanLibrary.tsx line 134: "+ Add Floor Plan"
- OptionLibrary.tsx line 155: "+ Add Option"
- OnboardingFormActions.tsx line 27: Form submit button

### 2. **Secondary/Outline Button** (Very Common)
**Used for:** Cancel actions, secondary/alternative flows
```
bg-white border-2 border-ink-muted text-ink-muted font-semibold px-6 py-3 rounded-lg hover:bg-gray-50 transition-colors ease-out disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
```
**Examples:**
- AddCommunityForm.tsx line 216: "Cancel" button
- OnboardingFormActions.tsx line 20: "Back" button

**Variant (with brand border):**
```
bg-white border-2 border-dashed border-brand text-brand hover:bg-brand hover:text-white font-semibold px-6 py-4 rounded-lg transition-colors ease-out
```
- AddCommunityForm.tsx line 234: "📁 Import Multiple Communities" link-style button

**Variant (with brand border, not dashed):**
```
bg-white border-2 border-brand text-brand hover:bg-orange-50 font-semibold px-6 py-2 rounded-lg transition-colors ease-out
```
- OptionLibrary.tsx line 149: "📤 Import from File"

### 3. **Text/Link Button** (Common for secondary actions)
**Used for:** Edit, inline actions, navigation links
```
text-brand hover:text-brand-hover font-medium
```
**Examples:**
- FloorPlanLibrary.tsx line 229: "Edit" button
- OptionLibrary.tsx line 288: "Edit" button
- WhatIfAnalysis.tsx line 66: "Refresh" button

### 4. **Danger/Destructive Button** (For deletions)
**Used for:** Delete actions, destructive operations
```
text-red-600 hover:text-red-700 font-medium
```
**Examples:**
- FloorPlanLibrary.tsx line 235: "Delete" button
- OptionLibrary.tsx line 294: "Delete" button

### 5. **Icon-Only/Closebutton** (Icon buttons in UI)
**Used for:** Close drawers, dismiss alerts, icon actions
```
p-1 rounded-md text-ink-muted hover:text-ink hover:bg-gray-100 transition-colors ease-out flex-shrink-0
```
**Example:**
- Drawer.tsx line 99: Close drawer button

### 6. **Muted/Secondary Button** (Less common, fallback)
**Used for:** Secondary background actions
```
bg-ink-muted hover:bg-ink text-white font-semibold py-3 rounded-lg transition-colors ease-out disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
```
**Example:**
- OnboardingFormActions.tsx line 20: "Back" button (alternative to outline)

---

## Key Design Patterns to Extract:

1. **Consistent padding:** `px-6 py-2` (small), `px-6 py-3` (standard), `px-6 py-4` (large/full-width)
2. **Always include:** `font-semibold` or `font-medium`, `rounded-lg`, `transition-colors ease-out`
3. **Disabled states:** Consistently use `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed`
4. **Hover effects:** Use design tokens (`hover:bg-brand-hover`) rather than hardcoded colors
5. **Border style:** Primary buttons use solid `border-2`, while outline buttons use `border-2 border-dashed` for imports

These patterns would map well to a Button component with variants: `primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `outline-dashed`, `text`, `danger`, and `icon`.

All 9 tasks complete. Let me do a final summary of everything that was changed.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Design system consistency payoff**: The 9 proposals touched ~30 files but followed a systematic pattern — each change aligns to a documented standard in AGENTS.md. The `statusClasses()` helper and `STATUS_ICON_COLORS` map create a single reference point for future status styling, while the `HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS` constant eliminates hex duplication for Recharts-specific colors. The key architectural insight: badge text needs `-700` shades for WCAG AA contrast, while icons can use the lighter design tokens — that's why the helper returns both.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

---

## Summary of All 9 Completed UI/UX Consistency Proposals

### Task 1: Replace `text-slate-*` with `text-ink-muted` tokens
**Status**: Already done in prior commits — verified no remaining `text-slate-*` instances.

### Task 2: Fix LoadingSpinner/LoadingState size mismatch
**File**: `src/components/ui/LoadingState.tsx`
- Fixed `sm` size from `w-6 h-6` (24px) to `w-4 h-4` (16px) to match LoadingSpinner.

### Task 3: Deduplicate health score band colors
**Files**: `src/lib/metricThresholds.ts`, `src/components/ui/BulletBar.tsx`
- Extracted `HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS` constant with hex values for Recharts SVG contexts.
- BulletBar now imports from the shared constant instead of hardcoding hex.

### Task 4: Add focus rings to interactive elements
**Files**: `src/components/ui/EmptyState.tsx`, `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`
- Added `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-brand/40 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-hidden` to CTA buttons and dismiss button.

### Task 5: Migrate CommunitiesList empty state
**File**: `src/components/communities/CommunitiesList.tsx`
- Replaced 20-line custom empty state with shared `<EmptyState>` component.

### Task 6: Standardize status colors (~30 files)
**New file**: `src/lib/statusColors.ts` — `statusClasses()` helper + `STATUS_ICON_COLORS` map.
**Files fixed**: Toast.tsx, ErrorDisplay.tsx, StatusIndicator.tsx, LoginForm.tsx, SignupForm.tsx, ChangeLog.tsx, CommunityJobLots.tsx, LegacyCommunityDashboard.tsx, CommunityFloorPlans.tsx, PricePositionIndicator.tsx, PropertyDashboard.tsx, ColumnMappingStep.tsx, PreviewValidationStep.tsx, LotSelector.tsx, OptionCheckboxes.tsx, MarketInsightsDisplay.tsx, DecisionFinalize.tsx.
- Standardized to: green-50/green-700, amber-50/amber-600, red-50/red-700, blue-100/blue-700.
- Icons use `text-status-*` design tokens.

### Task 7: Remap purple colors to info blue (~10 files)
**Files**: CommunityJobLots.tsx, EditCommunityForm.tsx, P3ScoreResults.tsx, P3WeightSliders.tsx, FloorPlanCards.tsx, OptionCheckboxes.tsx, DecisionFinalize.tsx, MarketInsightsDisplay.tsx, BrixAnalysisStep.tsx.
- All `purple-*` classes → `blue-*` equivalents. Zero purple remaining in non-demo code.

### Task 8: Consolidate ErrorDisplay components
**File**: `src/components/ui/ErrorDisplay.tsx`
- Extracted shared `ErrorIcon` component (eliminates duplicated SVG).
- Standardized all red shades to consistent `red-700` / `text-status-danger`.
- Kept `ErrorDisplay`, `ErrorCard`, `InlineError` exports unchanged for backward compatibility.

### Task 9: Extract shared Button component
**New file**: `src/components/ui/Button.tsx`
- 4 variants: `primary`, `secondary`, `text`, `danger`.
- 3 sizes: `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- Supports `href` prop (renders as `<a>`), `loading` state with spinner.
- Available for incremental adoption by new and existing screens.

**Verification**: TypeScript clean, 0 lint errors, 892/892 tests passing, production build succeeds.

**Key design decisions made during this audit:**
1. Status badge text uses Tailwind shade classes (`text-green-700`) rather than design tokens (`text-status-success`) because the tokens map to `-500` shades which don't meet WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast on `-50` backgrounds. Icons can use the tokens since they only need 3:1 (non-text).

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/coding/.claude/skills/codex-review

# Codex Review

Invoke OpenAI's Codex CLI to review the current branch, with instructions to research relevant documentation before reviewing.

## When to Use

- You want a second opinion on your implementation
- You want cross-verification between different AI models
- The implementation uses tools/libraries where current docs would help
- You've completed a feature and want thorough review before merging
- `/phase-checkpoint` invokes this for cross-model review (Step 4)

## Prerequisites

- Codex CLI installed (`codex --version` works)
- Valid OpenAI authentication (`codex login` completed)
- On a feature branch with commits to review

## Arguments

| Argument | Example | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `focus` | `security` | Focus review on specific area |
| `--upstream FILE` | `--upstream PRODUCT_SPEC.md` | Check that code preserves requirements from upstream doc |
| `--research TOPICS` | `--research "Supabase, NextAuth"` | Explicit technologies for Codex to research |
| `--base BRANCH` | `--base develop` | Compare against different base branch |
| `--model MODEL` | `--model gpt-5.2-codex` | Use specific Codex model |

## Workflow

Copy this checklist and track progress:

```
Codex Review Progress:
- [ ] Step 1: Verify Codex CLI available
- [ ] Step 2: Gather branch context
- [ ] Step 3: Generate review prompt
- [ ] Step 4: Invoke Codex
- [ ] Step 5: Present results
```

## Step 1: Verify Codex CLI

### Check if Running Inside Codex

```bash
# Codex sets CODEX_SANDBOX when running
if [ -n "$CODEX_SANDBOX" ]; then
  echo "RUNNING_IN_CODEX"
fi
```

**If running inside Codex CLI:**
```
CODEX REVIEW: SKIPPED
=====================
Reason: Already running inside Codex CLI.

Cross-model verification requires a different model.
Continuing without cross-model verification.
```

Return early. Do NOT block the parent workflow.

### Check Codex CLI Installed

```bash
codex --version
```

If not installed:
```
Codex CLI is not installed or not in PATH.

Install: https://github.com/openai/codex
Then run: codex login
```

### Check Authentication

```bash
codex login status
```

If not authenticated:
```
Codex authentication failed. Run:
  codex login
```

**If ANY pre-flight check fails:** Report the specific failure and STOP.
Do NOT attempt alternative commands or workarounds. Return status: `skipped`.

### Read Configuration

Read `.claude/settings.local.json` for settings:

```bash
# Read config
CODE_MODEL=$(jq -r '.codexReview.codeModel // "gpt-5.3-codex"' .claude/settings.local.json 2>/dev/null || echo "gpt-5.3-codex")
TIMEOUT_MINS=$(jq -r '.codexReview.reviewTimeoutMinutes // 20' .claude/settings.local.json 2>/dev/null || echo "20")
```

If `codexReview.enabled` is explicitly `false`, skip with message.

### Select Model

Priority order: `--model` flag > config > default (`gpt-5.3-codex`)

```bash
# 1. Explicit --model flag always wins
if [ -n "$EXPLICIT_MODEL" ]; then
  CODEX_MODEL="$EXPLICIT_MODEL"
# 2. Use configured code model
else
  CODEX_MODEL="$CODE_MODEL"
fi
```

**Note:** For reviewing non-code documents (specs, plans), use `/codex-consult` instead.

## Step 2: Gather Branch Context

Collect information about the current branch:

```bash
# Current branch name
git branch --show-current

# Commits on this branch (vs main or specified base)
BASE_BRANCH="${BASE:-main}"
git log --oneline $BASE_BRANCH..HEAD 2>/dev/null || git log --oneline -10

# Changed files summary
git diff $BASE_BRANCH...HEAD --stat 2>/dev/null || git diff HEAD~5 --stat

# Get the merge base
git merge-base $BASE_BRANCH HEAD 2>/dev/null
```

**Auto-detect research topics** from changed files if `--research` not provided:
- Check `package.json` for dependencies
- Look at import statements in changed files
- Identify frameworks (Next.js, React, etc.)

## Step 3: Generate Review Prompt

See [PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md](PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md) for the full prompt structure.

Key sections:
1. **Pre-Review Research** — Technologies Codex should research
2. **Review Context** — Branch, commits, changed files
3. **Upstream Context** (if `--upstream` provided) — Requirements to preserve
4. **Review Instructions** — What to check, output format

## Step 4: Invoke Codex

See [CODEX_INVOCATION.md](CODEX_INVOCATION.md) for detailed command building.

**IMPORTANT — Execution Rules:**
- Execute synchronously. NEVER use `run_in_background` for Codex invocations.
- If this command fails, report the exit code and return `status: error`.
  Do NOT retry with different flags or subcommands.
- Use the Bash tool's `timeout` parameter set to `TIMEOUT_MINS * 60 * 1000` (ms)
  instead of the shell `timeout` command or `run_in_background`.

### Safety Guard (prevent accidental commits)

Before invoking Codex, protect the working tree:

```bash
# Record current HEAD so we can detect if Codex makes commits
HEAD_BEFORE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Stash uncommitted changes (if any) to protect working tree
STASHED=false
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || ! git diff --cached --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
  git stash push -m "codex-review-safety-$(date +%s)" --include-untracked
  STASHED=true
fi
```

### Invoke Codex

```bash
OUTPUT_FILE="/tmp/codex-review-output-$(date +%s).txt"

# Build model flag
MODEL_FLAG=""
if [ -n "$CODEX_MODEL" ]; then
  MODEL_FLAG="--model $CODEX_MODEL"
fi

# Execute (use Bash tool's timeout parameter for timeout — NOT shell `timeout`)
cat {prompt_file} | codex exec \
  --sandbox danger-full-access \
  -c 'approval_policy="never"' \
  -c 'features.search=true' \
  $MODEL_FLAG \
  -o $OUTPUT_FILE \
  -
EXIT_CODE=$?
```

### Post-Invocation Safety Check

```bash
# Check if Codex made any commits
HEAD_AFTER=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
if [ "$HEAD_BEFORE" != "$HEAD_AFTER" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: Codex made commits during review. Reverting to pre-review state."
  git reset --hard "$HEAD_BEFORE"
fi

# Restore stashed changes
if [ "$STASHED" = true ]; then
  git stash pop
fi
```

**Flags explained:**
- `--sandbox danger-full-access`: Enables network access for documentation research
- `-c 'approval_policy="never"'`: Non-interactive execution
- `-c 'features.search=true'`: Enable web search for documentation research
- `-o $OUTPUT_FILE`: Write final response to file for reliable parsing
- `-`: Read prompt from stdin

**Important:** Do NOT use `2>&1` — Codex streams progress to stderr and final output to stdout. Merging them corrupts the parseable response.

## Step 5: Present Results

Parse and present the Codex output. See [EVALUATION_PRACTICES.md](EVALUATION_PRACTICES.md) for severity classification.

### Output Format (User-Facing)

```
CODEX REVIEW COMPLETE
=====================
Branch: feature/add-auth
Reviewed by: Codex ({model})
Status: PASS WITH NOTES

Critical Issues: None

Recommendations:
1. [src/auth/handler.ts:45] Consider adding rate limiting
   → Suggestion: Use express-rate-limit middleware

2. [src/auth/session.ts:12] Session expiry not explicitly configured
   → Suggestion: Add explicit maxAge to session config

Positive Findings:
- Good separation of concerns in auth module
- Proper error handling for OAuth failures

{If --upstream provided}
Context Preservation: ✓ All 5 items from PRODUCT_SPEC.md preserved
{/If}
```

### Output Format (Programmatic — for /phase-checkpoint)

When invoked by another skill, return structured data:

```json
{
  "status": "pass | pass_with_notes | needs_attention | error | skipped",
  "critical_issues": [],
  "recommendations": [],
  "positive_findings": [],
  "context_preservation": {
    "checked": true,
    "all_preserved": true,
    "missing_items": []
  }
}
```

## Error Handling

| Failure | Action |
|---------|--------|
| Codex CLI not found | Report and stop |
| Authentication failed | Suggest `codex login` |
| No commits on branch | Report nothing to review |
| Codex times out | Return partial output if available |
| Output is malformed | Attempt best-effort parsing: extract any text between known markers (e.g., "Critical Issues:", "Recommendations:"). If no structure found, return the raw output as a single recommendation with status `pass_with_notes` and note "Codex output could not be parsed — raw response included" |

## Configuration

Read from `.claude/settings.local.json`:

```json
{
  "codexReview": {
    "enabled": true,
    "codeModel": "gpt-5.3-codex",
    "reviewTimeoutMinutes": 20
  }
}
```

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | `true` | Set to `false` to disable Codex review |
| `codeModel` | `"gpt-5.3-codex"` | Model for code review tasks |
| `reviewTimeoutMinutes` | `20` | Max time for review invocations |

For document consultation (specs, plans), see `/codex-consult` which uses `codexConsult` config.
For task execution via Codex, see `/phase-start --codex` which uses `codexReview.taskTimeoutMinutes`.

**For CI/headless environments:** Set `CODEX_API_KEY` environment variable for authentication without interactive login.

## Examples

**Basic review:**
```
/codex-review
```

**Focus on security:**
```
/codex-review security
```

**Verify against upstream spec:**
```
/codex-review --upstream PRODUCT_SPEC.md
```

**Explicit research topics:**
```
/codex-review --research "Supabase Auth, Next.js App Router"
```

**Different base branch and model:**
```
/codex-review --base develop --model gpt-5.2-codex
```

# Codex Review Prompt Template

Template for the prompt sent to Codex CLI.

## Structure

```markdown
# Pre-Review Research (REQUIRED)

Before reviewing the code, research the following documentation:

{For each item in research_topics or auto-detected technologies}
- **{topic}**: Find current official documentation and best practices

{If project has CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or similar}
- **Project patterns**: Review coding standards from project documentation

# Review Context

Branch: `{branch_name}`
Base: `{base_branch}`
Commits: {commit_count} commits

## Commits on this branch:
{commit_list from git log}

## Changed Files:
{file_list from git diff --stat}

{If --upstream provided}
# Upstream Context

This code should preserve requirements from:
- {upstream_file}

Check that nothing important was lost or incorrectly implemented.

Key requirements to verify:
{extracted requirements from upstream file}
{/If}

{If focus area provided}
# Focus Area

Pay special attention to: {focus_area}
{/If}

# Review Instructions

Provide a thorough code review covering:

1. **Correctness**: Logic errors, edge cases, potential bugs
2. **Best Practices**: Does the code follow established patterns?
3. **Consistency**: Are changes applied consistently across files?
4. **Documentation**: Are changes well-documented where needed?
5. **Potential Issues**: Security, performance, maintainability concerns

Use `git diff {base_branch}...HEAD` to see the full changes.

Provide specific file:line references for any issues found.

## Output Format

Provide findings in this exact format:

```
REVIEW FINDINGS
===============
Branch: {branch}
Status: PASS | PASS_WITH_NOTES | NEEDS_ATTENTION

CRITICAL ISSUES (blocking)
--------------------------
{List issues that must be addressed, or "None"}

Each issue format:
- [file:line] Description
  → Suggestion: How to fix

RECOMMENDATIONS (non-blocking)
------------------------------
{List suggestions for improvement, or "None"}

POSITIVE FINDINGS
-----------------
{What was done well}

{If upstream context provided}
CONTEXT PRESERVATION
--------------------
- Requirements checked: {N}
- All preserved: Yes/No
- Missing/incorrect: {list or "None"}
{/If}
```

Be specific. Reference line numbers. Prioritize by impact.
```

## Auto-Detection of Research Topics

When `--research` is not provided, auto-detect from:

1. **package.json** — Look for key dependencies:
   - `next` → "Next.js App Router"
   - `@supabase/supabase-js` → "Supabase"
   - `stripe` → "Stripe API"
   - `@auth/core` → "Auth.js"

2. **Changed files** — Check imports:
   - React hooks → "React Hooks"
   - API routes → "Next.js API Routes"
   - Database queries → relevant ORM docs

3. **File types** — Suggest based on extensions:
   - `.prisma` → "Prisma ORM"
   - `.graphql` → "GraphQL"

## Upstream Context Extraction

When `--upstream` is provided:

1. Read the upstream file
2. Extract numbered requirements, acceptance criteria, or key decisions
3. Include in prompt for Codex to verify against
4. Request explicit confirmation of each item in output

# Codex CLI Invocation

Detailed instructions for invoking Codex CLI for review.

## Execution Rules (MANDATORY)

1. **NEVER use `run_in_background`** — Always execute Codex synchronously.
   Background execution generates delayed notifications for every attempt,
   creating noise for the user.

2. **NEVER retry with modified syntax** — If the command fails, report the
   exit code and skip. Do NOT try alternative subcommands, flag combinations,
   or workarounds.

3. **Use the EXACT command documented below** — Do not improvise flags,
   rearrange arguments, or substitute subcommands (e.g. do not switch
   from `codex exec` to `codex review`).

## Safety Guard (Prevent Accidental Commits)

Codex runs with `--sandbox danger-full-access` for network access but this also
grants write access to the working tree. The safety guard prevents Codex from
making unintended commits during review.

```bash
# Record HEAD before Codex runs
HEAD_BEFORE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Stash uncommitted changes to protect working tree
STASHED=false
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || ! git diff --cached --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
  git stash push -m "codex-review-safety-$(date +%s)" --include-untracked
  STASHED=true
fi
```

## Build Command

```bash
# Create output file path
OUTPUT_FILE="/tmp/codex-review-output-$(date +%s).txt"

# Read config (model selection handled by SKILL.md Step 1)
CODEX_MODEL=$(jq -r '.codexReview.codeModel // empty' .claude/settings.local.json 2>/dev/null)
TIMEOUT_MINS=$(jq -r '.codexReview.reviewTimeoutMinutes // 10' .claude/settings.local.json 2>/dev/null || echo "10")

# Build model flag if configured
MODEL_FLAG=""
if [ -n "$CODEX_MODEL" ]; then
  MODEL_FLAG="--model $CODEX_MODEL"
fi

# Execute (use Bash tool's timeout parameter for timeout — NOT shell `timeout`)
cat {prompt_file} | codex exec \
  --sandbox danger-full-access \
  -c 'approval_policy="never"' \
  -c 'features.search=true' \
  $MODEL_FLAG \
  -o $OUTPUT_FILE \
  -
EXIT_CODE=$?

# --- Post-Invocation Safety Check ---
# Revert any commits Codex may have made
HEAD_AFTER=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
if [ "$HEAD_BEFORE" != "$HEAD_AFTER" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: Codex made commits during review. Reverting."
  git reset --hard "$HEAD_BEFORE"
fi

# Restore stashed changes
if [ "$STASHED" = true ]; then
  git stash pop
fi
# --- End Safety Check ---

# Handle exit codes
if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 124 ]; then
  # Timeout - return partial output if available
  CODEX_STATUS="error"
  CODEX_REASON="Timeout after ${TIMEOUT_MINS} minutes"
elif [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]; then
  # Error - log and return error status
  CODEX_STATUS="error"
  CODEX_REASON="Codex exited with code $EXIT_CODE"
fi

# Read output
if [ -f "$OUTPUT_FILE" ]; then
  CODEX_OUTPUT=$(cat "$OUTPUT_FILE")
  rm -f "$OUTPUT_FILE"
else
  CODEX_STATUS="error"
  CODEX_REASON="No output file produced"
fi
```

## Flags Explained

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--sandbox danger-full-access` | Enables network access for documentation research |
| `-c 'approval_policy="never"'` | Non-interactive execution |
| `-c 'features.search=true'` | Enable web search for documentation research |
| `--model` | Optional, use configured model or Codex default |
| `-o $OUTPUT_FILE` | Write final response to file for parsing |
| `-` | Read prompt from stdin |

## Important Notes

**Do NOT use `2>&1`** — Codex streams progress to stderr and final output to stdout. Merging them corrupts the parseable response.

**Timeout:** Use configured timeout (default: 10 minutes). Codex may need time to research.

## Failure Handling

- **WCAG AA Contrast Requirements**: Research 4.5:1 ratio for text, 3:1 for non-text elements — verify color choices in badges and icons

## Summary of Changes

This is a comprehensive UI/UX consistency audit implementing 9 proposals:

1. **text-slate-* → text-ink-muted**: Replace 4 instances of text-slate-400/600 with the app's `text-ink-muted` design token (BulletBar.tsx, RadialRing.tsx, CommunityHealthWidget.tsx)

2. **LoadingState size alignment**: LoadingState sm was w-6 h-6 (24px), LoadingSpinner sm is w-4 h-4 (16px). Changed LoadingState sm to w-4 h-4 to match.

3. **HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS extraction**: Duplicate hex values (#fee2e2, #fef9c3, #d1fae5) in BulletBar.tsx now import from a shared `HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS` constant in metricThresholds.ts.

4. **Focus rings on EmptyState/Toast**: Added `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-brand/40 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-hidden` to interactive elements in EmptyState.tsx (CTA button and link) and Toast.tsx (dismiss button).

5. **CommunitiesList → shared EmptyState**: Replaced 25-line custom empty state with the shared `<EmptyState>` component.

6. **Status color standardization** (~20 files): Normalized inconsistent status color shades across the app:
   - Success: bg-green-50 / text-green-700 (was: green-100, green-500, green-600, green-800)
   - Warning: bg-amber-50 / text-amber-600 (was: yellow-100, orange-100, amber-700, amber-800)
   - Danger: bg-red-50 / text-red-700 (was: red-100, red-500, red-600, red-800)
   - Info: bg-blue-100 / text-blue-700 (was: blue-500, blue-800)
   - Icons use design tokens (text-status-success, text-status-danger, etc.) which map to -500 shades — acceptable for non-text (3:1 ratio)

Affected: P3ScoreResults, MarketInsightsDisplay, P3WeightSliders, EditCommunityForm, FloorPlanCards, CommunityJobLots, DecisionFinalize, OptionCheckboxes, BrixAnalysisStep.

   - 4 variants: primary, secondary, text, danger
   - 3 sizes: sm, md, lg
   - `loading` prop with spinner
   - Polymorphic: renders `<a>` when `href` provided, `<button>` otherwise
   - Uses discriminated union types (AsButton | AsAnchor)

- `statusClasses(level)` — returns { bg, text, border } for badge styling

### src/lib/statusColors.ts
```typescript
export type StatusLevel = 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'neutral';

export function statusClasses(level: StatusLevel): { bg: string; text: string; border: string } {
  switch (level) {
    case 'success': return { bg: 'bg-green-50', text: 'text-green-700', border: 'border-green-200' };
    case 'warning': return { bg: 'bg-amber-50', text: 'text-amber-600', border: 'border-amber-200' };
    case 'danger': return { bg: 'bg-red-50', text: 'text-red-700', border: 'border-red-200' };
    case 'info': return { bg: 'bg-blue-100', text: 'text-blue-700', border: 'border-blue-200' };
    case 'neutral': return { bg: 'bg-gray-100', text: 'text-gray-500', border: 'border-gray-200' };
  }
}

export const STATUS_ICON_COLORS: Record<StatusLevel, string> = {
  success: 'text-status-success',
  warning: 'text-status-warning',
  danger: 'text-status-danger',
  info: 'text-status-info',
  neutral: 'text-status-neutral',
};
```

Uses discriminated union types to support both `<button>` and `<a>` rendering:
- `AsButton` type: `href?: never` (forces button rendering)
- `AsAnchor` type: `href: string` (forces anchor rendering)
- Variants use the app's design tokens: bg-brand, text-ink, etc.

The app uses Tailwind CSS v4 with design tokens defined via `@theme` in `src/styles/global.css`:
- `text-ink` (#2C3E50) for body text
- `text-ink-muted` (#5A6C7D) for secondary text
- `bg-brand` (#FA4616) for primary actions
- `text-status-success` (#10B981), `text-status-warning` (#F59E0B), `text-status-danger` (#EF4444), `text-status-info` (#3B82F6), `text-status-neutral` (#6B7280) for status

- Success: bg-green-50 text-status-success
- Warning: bg-amber-50 text-status-warning
- Danger: bg-red-50 text-status-danger
- Info: bg-blue-100 text-status-info
- Neutral: bg-gray-100 text-status-neutral

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

**Spec section:** Metric Click-Through Drawer — Drillable metric affordance pattern

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.
## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.
## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview
**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted
## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. ## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.

Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

Branch: `main`

## Summary of Changes

This is a comprehensive UI/UX consistency audit implementing 9 proposals:

1. **text-slate → text-ink-muted**: Replace instances of text-slate-400/600 with the app's text-ink-muted design token
2. **LoadingState size alignment**: LoadingState sm was w-6 h-6 (24px), changed to w-4 h-4 to match LoadingSpinner sm
3. **HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS extraction**: Duplicate hex values now import from shared constant in metricThresholds.ts
4. **Focus rings on EmptyState/Toast**: Added focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-brand/40 to interactive elements

6. **Status color standardization** (~20 files): Normalized to green-50/700, amber-50/600, red-50/700, blue-100/700
7. **Purple → blue remapping** (~10 files): Eliminated all purple usage, remapped to blue/info palette
8. **ErrorDisplay consolidation**: Extracted shared ErrorIcon component with size prop
9. **Button component extraction**: New Button.tsx with 4 variants, 3 sizes, loading state, polymorphic rendering

New files: src/lib/statusColors.ts, src/components/ui/Button.tsx

## Design System Context

The app uses Tailwind CSS v4 with design tokens defined via @theme in global.css.
Status tokens (text-status-success etc.) map to -500 shades (~3.2:1 contrast on -50 bg).
Badge TEXT uses -700 shades (5.5:1+ for WCAG AA). ICONS use tokens (3:1 OK for non-text).

Info uniquely uses bg-blue-100 (not -50) per AGENTS.md standard.

# Remove entire top metric card bar from portfolio overview

**Date:** 2026-02-15
**Spec section:** Portfolio Overview
**Status:** Accepted

## Context
KIN-39: David found confusion between daily carry cost ($6,800) and monthly exposure ($11,400) on the portfolio overview page. While scoping the fix, we audited all three top-level metric cards (Active Specs, Inventory Value, Daily Carry Cost) against the PortfolioSummaryCard that sits directly below them.

## Considered
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost only**: Keep 2-card top bar (Active Specs + Inventory Value). Minimal change but Inventory Value remains duplicated with PortfolioSummaryCard.
- **Remove Daily Carry Cost + Inventory Value**: Reduce to 1 top card (Active Specs). Awkward single-card row.
- **Remove entire top bar**: Eliminate all 3 top metric cards. PortfolioSummaryCard already shows Inventory Value and Exposure at Risk. Active Specs link exists in top nav.

## Decision
Remove the entire top metric card bar. The PortfolioSummaryCard becomes the sole portfolio-level summary. Rationale:
- Eliminates all duplication (Inventory Value shown in both tiers)
- Removes the confusing daily carry figure entirely rather than moving it
- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

Changed: 30 files, 245 insertions, 131 deletions

## Summary of Changes

This is a comprehensive UI/UX consistency audit implementing 9 proposals:

1. **text-slate → text-ink-muted**: Replace instances of text-slate-400/600 with the app's text-ink-muted design token
2. **LoadingState size alignment**: LoadingState sm was w-6 h-6 (24px), changed to w-4 h-4 to match LoadingSpinner sm
3. **HEALTH_SCORE_BANDS extraction**: Duplicate hex values now import from shared constant in metricThresholds.ts

7. **Purple → blue remapping** (~10 files): Eliminated all purple usage, remapped to blue/info palette
8. **ErrorDisplay consolidation**: Extracted shared ErrorIcon component with size prop
9. **Button component extraction**: New Button.tsx with 4 variants, 3 sizes, loading state, polymorphic rendering

New files: src/lib/statusColors.ts, src/components/ui/Button.tsx

## Design System Context

The app uses Tailwind CSS v4 with design tokens defined via @theme in global.css.
Status tokens (text-status-success etc.) map to -500 shades (~3.2:1 contrast on -50 bg).
Badge TEXT uses -700 shades (5.5:1+ for WCAG AA). ICONS use tokens (3:1 OK for non-text).

Info uniquely uses bg-blue-100 (not -50) per AGENTS.md standard.

**Status:** Accepted

- Simplifies the page hierarchy: one summary card, then priority-sorted community list

# AGENTS.md - KineticBI Project

This is the single source of truth for AI coding agents working on this repository.

---

## Tapestry — Living Specification

This project maintains a living specification in `.tapestry/`. The tapestry is the authoritative source of product intent, decisions, and context. It compounds over time — every session should leave it richer than you found it. If `.tapestry/` is missing or empty, skip — tapestry is optional until initialized.

### At session start

1. Read `.tapestry/spec.md` to understand what this product is and what it should do.
2. Scan `.tapestry/questions/open/` — if any open questions are relevant to your work, note them. If you can answer one based on what you discover, draft a resolution.
3. Skim recent files in `.tapestry/decisions/` and `.tapestry/sessions/` for context on recent work and choices.

### During work

- **Architectural/design decisions**: Create a file in `.tapestry/decisions/` using `.tapestry/templates/decision.md`. Name it `NNN-short-slug.md` (next number after highest existing).
- **Spec ambiguity or gaps**: Create a file in `.tapestry/questions/open/` using `.tapestry/templates/question.md`. Name it `qNNN-short-slug.md`. Do not guess — file the question and work around it.
- **Spec needs updating**: Create a file in `.tapestry/pending/` using `.tapestry/templates/pending-update.md`. Name it `update-NNN-short-slug.md`. **Do not modify `.tapestry/spec.md` directly.**
- **What NOT to log**: Routine implementation details, obvious decisions, questions answerable from existing spec + decisions. Log only things a future session would benefit from knowing.

### At session end

Create a session summary in `.tapestry/sessions/` using `.tapestry/templates/session.md`. Name it `YYYY-MM-DD-short-slug.md`. Keep it concise.

---

## Agent Instructions

### Task Execution
- Read the full task description and acceptance criteria before starting
- Complete all acceptance criteria before marking a task done
- As work is completed, check off the corresponding items in any execution plan

### General Guardrails
- Make the smallest change that passes tests and improves the code
- Do not duplicate templates or files to work around issues—fix the original
- Respect privacy: do not log secrets, prompts, completions, or PII
- Work in git branches. Check if you're on main, and prompt the human to create a new branch if needed

### When Stuck
- If a file cannot be opened, content is missing, or a test fails unexpectedly, say so explicitly and stop
- Do not guess or work around
- Read the full error output before attempting fixes—the answer is usually in the stack trace

### Ross MVP Specific
- **Staging tables only:** Do not create "production" tables—all data lives in `staging_*` tables for MVP
- **Short codes are king:** Community identification uses short codes (3-5 letter abbreviations like AUCES, FOCRS), not UUIDs
- **Sales data available:** After Sprint 2, Pace vs Budget and Backlog metrics use `staging_sales_transactions` table
- **Metric thresholds:** Color coding uses configurable thresholds in `src/lib/metricThresholds.ts`—these are placeholder values that can be adjusted
- **Avg Age vs DOM:** "Avg Age of Inventory" replaced "Days on Market" in Sprint 2 (no MLS dependency)
- **Blocked metrics:** Gross Profit requires cost data we don't have—always show "—" placeholder

---

## Testing Policy (Non-Negotiable)

### Core Rules
- Tests **MUST** cover the functionality being implemented
- **NEVER** ignore the output of the system or the tests—logs often contain critical information
- **NEVER** disable functionality to hide a failure—fix root cause
- **NEVER** claim something is "working" when any functionality is disabled or broken

### What "Green Tests" Means
All configured checks must pass:
1. TypeScript type checking passes (`npm run typecheck`)
2. Linting passes (`npm run lint`)
3. Build succeeds (`npm run build`)
4. Unit tests pass (`npm run test`)

A step is not complete until all checks pass.

---

## Project Overview

KineticBI Dashboard - SaaS application for small and medium homebuilders to manage communities and properties. Built with Astro (SSR mode), React, and Supabase.

**Live App:** `app.kineticbi.com`
**Related Repos:**
- Landing Page: `github.com/matthewbostwick/kineticbi-landing` - Marketing site at `www.kineticbi.com`

**Current Phase**: All-in carry cost model (KIN-24) shipped. UI design tokens, shared components, and tech debt refactoring complete (PRs #57–#61).

---

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: Astro 5.14 (Server-Side Rendering)
- **UI Components**: React 19
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS 4
- **Authentication**: Supabase Auth
- **Database**: Supabase PostgreSQL
- **Hosting**: Netlify (serverless functions)
- **Data Grid**: Tailwind-native DataGrid component (CSS Grid, typed columns, search, sort)
- **File Parsing**: xlsx (SheetJS) for CSV/Excel imports
- **AI Services**: Claude only (Anthropic)
  - Claude Sonnet 4 (batch market research via Trigger.dev)
  - Claude 3.5 Haiku (real-time score explanations)
- **Background Jobs**: Trigger.dev v4 (scheduled market research)
- **Analytics**: PostHog (product analytics, error tracking)

---

## Development Commands

```bash
npm install           # Install dependencies
cp .env.example .env  # Create environment file (add Supabase credentials)
npm run dev           # Development server at http://localhost:4321
npm run build         # Production build
npm run preview       # Preview production build
npm run test          # Run tests
npm run typecheck     # TypeScript type checking
npm run lint          # ESLint
```

---

## Architecture Overview

### Authentication Flow
- `/` - Login page (email/password and magic link)
- `/signup` - User registration
- `/auth/callback` - OAuth and magic link handler
- Middleware at `/src/middleware.ts` handles route protection and session validation

### Onboarding Flow
New users complete a 3-step onboarding after signup:
1. `/onboarding/personal` - Name and role collection
2. `/onboarding/business` - Company details
3. Auto-redirect to `/overview` on completion

### Middleware Routing Logic (src/middleware.ts)
Critical routing rules enforced server-side:
1. **Public routes**: `/`, `/signup`, `/auth/callback` - No auth required
2. **Onboarding routes**: `/onboarding/*` - Requires auth, redirects to overview if completed
3. **Protected routes**: All other routes require authentication + completed onboarding
4. **Session validation**: Validates session tokens from cookies on every request

---

## API Endpoint Patterns

**Always use `apiHelpers` pattern** for consistency and Netlify compatibility:

```typescript
import { getAuthenticatedClient, unauthorizedResponse, errorResponse, successResponse } from '../../../lib/apiHelpers';

export const GET: APIRoute = async (context) => {
  const auth = await getAuthenticatedClient(context);
  if (!auth) return unauthorizedResponse();

  const { supabase, user } = auth;
  // ... your query logic
  return successResponse(data);
};
```

**Avoid**: `createServerClient` from `@supabase/ssr` - doesn't work reliably in Netlify Functions

---

## UI Patterns

**Complex Forms**: Use dedicated page routes, not modals
- Good: `/communities/[id]/floor-plans/assign` (dedicated page)
- Good: `/admin/options/import` (4-step import wizard)
- Avoid: `<AssignFloorPlanModal>` (Radix Portal + Astro SSR causes hydration issues)

**Simple Interactions**: Modals are fine for delete confirmations, single-field inputs

**DataGrid**: Use `<DataGrid>` from `src/components/ui/DataGrid.tsx` for tabular data with sorting, search, and truncation tooltips. Columns are defined via `DataGridColumn<T>[]` with typed generics.
- **Column API**: `render(row, value, i)` for custom cells, `format(value, row)` for display strings, `getValue(row, i)` for raw values, `headerRender()` for custom headers.
- **Sort**: Single-column sort with null-to-end. Set `defaultSort: 'asc' | 'desc'` on one column. Uses `useSortedData()` hook from `src/hooks/useDataGrid.ts`.
- **Search**: Debounced (200ms), matches both raw and formatted values. Enable with `searchable` prop.
- **Row styling**: Use `getRowClass(row, i)` prop for conditional row backgrounds (e.g., Garman highlight in CommunityMarket).
- **PostHog**: `datagrid_sorted` and `datagrid_searched` events fire automatically.

**TabBar**: Use `<TabBar>` from `src/components/ui/TabBar.tsx` for segment-control tabs. Renders as a pill-shaped toggle (bg-gray-100 container, white active state with shadow). Props: `tabs` (array of `{id, label, count?, icon?}`), `activeTab`, `onChange`, `size` (`'sm'` | `'md'`). Uses `role="tab"` and `aria-selected` for accessibility.

**Tooltip**: Use `<Tooltip>` from `src/components/ui/Tooltip.tsx` for dark-background hover tooltips. Props: `content` (ReactNode), `children`, `position` (`'top'` | `'bottom'` | `'left'` | `'right'`), `width`. Uses CSS-only visibility toggle via Tailwind group-hover.

**Breadcrumb**: Use `<Breadcrumb>` from `src/components/ui/Breadcrumb.tsx` for in-layout path navigation. Props: `items` (array of `{label, href?}`). Renders `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` + `<ol>` and applies `aria-current="page"` to the final item. Tracks `breadcrumb_clicked` on link clicks.

**EmptyState**: Use `<EmptyState>` from `src/components/ui/EmptyState.tsx` for empty-data views instead of ad-hoc placeholders. Props: `icon?`, `message`, `description?`, `action?`, `component?`. Includes `role="status"` and tracks `empty_state_shown`.

**Cross-Island Communication**: Dashboard breadcrumb context is passed from child React islands to `DashboardLayout` via `window` `CustomEvent` (`breadcrumb-context`), not React Context (React Context does not cross Astro island boundaries).

**Status Badges**: Use consistent status colors across the app:
- Success/Active: `bg-green-50 text-status-success`
- Warning/Reserved: `bg-amber-50 text-status-warning`
- Danger/Critical: `bg-red-50 text-status-danger`
- Info/In Development: `bg-blue-100 text-status-info`
- Neutral/Sold/Default: `bg-gray-100 text-status-neutral`

**Badge Variants**: Two standard shapes:
- Pill: `rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium`
- Rectangular: `rounded px-2.5 py-1 text-sm font-semibold`

---

## PostHog Analytics

**IMPORTANT**: All new features MUST include PostHog analytics tracking.

### Usage Pattern

```typescript
import { initPostHog, trackEvent, trackError } from '../../lib/posthog';

useEffect(() => {
  initPostHog();
  trackEvent('my_feature_viewed');
}, []);

// Track events: trackEvent('feature_action', { step: 'name', count: 5 });
// Track errors: trackError('feature_failed', error, { context: 'info' });
```

### Event Naming Convention
Use snake_case: `{feature}_{action}` (e.g., `brix_import_started`, `community_created`)

---

## AI Features Architecture

### What-If / Diagnostics Pipeline (PR #56, KIN-24)
- **Diagnostics API** (`/api/what-if/diagnostics`) is the single authority for comp data — fetches, validates, enriches, IQR-trims comps, and computes market position.
- **Predict API** (`/api/what-if/predict`) is pure computation — returns `propertySituation` (with carry cost breakdown), `marginInputBase`, and `spec` only (response v3). No comp data.
- **Frontend** sources comp data from `DiagnosticSummary` callback (not the predict response).
- **Comp service** (`src/lib/compService.ts`) wraps the `find_property_comps()` RPC — all callers import from here, no inline RPC calls.
- **What-If engine** (`src/lib/whatIfEngine.ts`) handles all scenario computation locally after a single fetch on mount.
- **Carry cost model** (KIN-24): Two components — Loan Carry (12% annual) and Other Carry (2.5% annual + $850/mo flat). `dailyCarryCost()` helper is the shared entry point for all carry computations. SQL-side uses `carry_cost_daily()` helper.
- **Overview metrics**: Single RPC — `compute_portfolio_performance()` returns portfolio + community performance data including `totalDailyCarryCost`. The former `overview_metrics()` function has been dropped; the API route maps `totalActiveUnits` → `activeSpecs`, `totalInventoryValue` → `inventoryValue`, `totalDailyCarryCost` → `dailyCarryCost`.

### Two-Layer Architecture
1. **Batch Layer** (Trigger.dev + Claude Sonnet 4) - Pre-compute market research by zipcode
2. **Real-Time Layer** (Claude 3.5 Haiku) - Personalized explanations using cached research

### Batch Research Jobs
Located in `/trigger/jobs/`: real-estate.ts, employers.ts, demographics.ts, anchors.ts, amenities.ts, summarize.ts, snapshot-comps.ts

**Trigger.dev Dashboard**: https://cloud.trigger.dev
**Project**: `proj_fevlpavilsqtkoyocatf`

### Real-Time API Endpoints
- `POST /api/ai/explain-scores` - P3 score explanations
- `GET /api/ai/market-insights?zipcode=` - Cached market analysis

---

## Brand Guidelines

### Design Tokens (Tailwind)

All brand colors are mapped to Tailwind utilities via `@theme` in `src/styles/global.css`. **Always use tokens instead of hardcoded hex:**

| Hex | Token class | Usage |
|-----|------------|-------|
| `#2C3E50` | `text-ink` | Headlines, body text |
| `#5A6C7D` | `text-ink-muted` | Secondary text, labels |
| `#FA4616` | `text-brand`, `bg-brand`, `border-brand` | Primary actions, links |
| `#FF6B3D` | `hover:text-brand-hover`, `hover:bg-brand-hover` | Hover states |
| `#F7F9FB` | `bg-surface` | Card/section backgrounds |
| `#10B981` | `text-status-success`, `bg-status-success` | Success indicators |
| `#F59E0B` | `text-status-warning`, `bg-status-warning` | Warning indicators |
| `#EF4444` | `text-status-danger`, `bg-status-danger` | Danger/error indicators |
| `#3B82F6` | `text-status-info`, `bg-status-info` | Informational indicators |
| `#6B7280` | `text-status-neutral`, `bg-status-neutral` | Neutral/default indicators |

**Exception:** Recharts components (`fill`, `stroke`, `style` props) require literal hex values — CSS custom properties don't work in SVG attributes.

### Z-Index Scale
- `z-10`: Sticky headers, in-page overlays
- `z-20`: Dropdown menus, popovers
- `z-40`: Drawers, slide-out panels
- `z-50`: Modals, dialogs
- `z-[60]`: Toasts, notifications
- `z-[70]`: Tooltips (always on top)

### Key Messaging
**Primary Tagline:** "Finally, spec intelligence built for builders like you."
**Target Audience:** Small to medium homebuilders (1-50 person teams) managing multiple communities.

## Deployment

## Dev Automation Login (Local)

Browser automation (Playwright / Chrome DevTools MCP) can use `GET /api/dev/login` to establish a cookie session without manual UI steps.

- Set in `.env.local`: `DEV_LOGIN_EMAIL`, `DEV_LOGIN_PASSWORD` (optional: `DEV_LOGIN_TOKEN`)
- Visit: `http://localhost:4321/api/dev/login` (or `...?token=...` if token is set) → redirects to `/overview` with cookies set
- Requires local Supabase running and `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` / `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` configured
- If `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is present, the endpoint will auto-provision/confirm the dev user and can reset password drift

## Database

### Schema
See [docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md](docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md) for full table definitions, RPC functions, and migration commands.

### Migration Workflow
See [docs/DATABASE_MIGRATIONS.md](docs/DATABASE_MIGRATIONS.md) for creating, applying, and managing migrations safely.

**Key rules** (always apply):
- NEVER modify existing migration files after they've been applied
- NEVER use `supabase db reset` — it wipes all data
- Local DB access: `docker exec -i supabase_db_KineticBI psql -U postgres -d postgres`
- All tables have RLS policies and are user-scoped via `user_id`

---

## Commit Messages

Format: `<scope>: <description>`

| Scope | Use |
|-------|-----|
| `feat` | New functionality |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `test` | Test additions/changes |
| `refactor` | Code restructuring |
| `docs` | Documentation |
| `chore` | Build/tooling changes |
| `db` | Database migrations |

Examples: `feat(api): add communities metrics endpoint`, `fix(overview): handle empty community data`

---

## Git Branch Strategy

Create one branch per **phase** (not per step or task): `git checkout -b phase-{N}`
Do not push until human reviews at checkpoint.

See [docs/GIT_WORKFLOW.md](docs/GIT_WORKFLOW.md) for branch lifecycle, task commit format, and phase PR process.

---

## When to Ask for Human Input

Ask the human if any of the following is true:
- You need new environment variables or secrets
- An external dependency or major architectural change is required
- A test is failing and you cannot determine why after reading the full error output
- Manual verification requires credentials or external services you cannot access
- The task requires data from a Ross document that isn't in the staging tables
- You're unsure about community short code mappings

---

## Follow-Up Items

During development, track discovered items outside current scope in `TODOS.md`:
- Do NOT silently ignore discovered issues
- Do NOT scope-creep by fixing them without approval
- Track in TODOS.md and let the human decide
- Include enough context that the item is actionable later

See [docs/TODO_WORKFLOW.md](docs/TODO_WORKFLOW.md) for templates and categories.

---

Before marking any task complete:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria met
- [ ] Type checking passes
- [ ] No lint errors
- [ ] Build succeeds
- [ ] Tests pass
- [ ] Browser verification done (if required)
- [ ] Commit message follows format
- [ ] Changes are minimal and focused

See [docs/VERIFICATION_WORKFLOW.md](docs/VERIFICATION_WORKFLOW.md) for detailed verification steps, including code-verification skill usage, browser verification checklists, and phase checkpoint processes.

# KineticBI Project Memory

## Architecture Patterns
- What-If engine: Single fetch on mount, all slider/incentive changes compute locally via `generateScenarios()`
- IQR outlier trimming in `computeMarketPosition()` — Q1-2.0*IQR to Q3+2.0*IQR (k=2.0 for skewed data)
  - Safeguards: n≥10 gate, min-retained floor of 5, IQR=0 bypass (aligned with SQL)
- **Active Spec Definition** (4 conditions): `spec_model = 'Spec'`, `sold_date IS NULL`, `not_for_sale` is null/false, `days_in_inv IS NOT NULL`
  - Canonical SQL helper: `get_community_active_specs()` — `p_active_only=false` skips active filters
  - 7 live locations: SQL helper, `compute_portfolio_performance()`, `active-specs.ts`, `properties.ts`, `computeOverviewMetrics.ts`, `snapshot-comps.ts`, `metrics.ts` (fallback via computeOverviewMetrics)
  - Skipped: `scripts/compare-staging-tables.ts` (one-time validation script)
- API pattern: `withAuth` wrapper from `apiHelpers.ts`, not raw Supabase SSR client
- Comp search: `src/lib/compService.ts` is the single source of truth for `find_property_comps()` RPC
  - `RpcCompRow` = canonical 36-field type matching SQL RETURNS TABLE
  - `fetchComps()`, `fetchCompsBothModes()`, `fetchMlsMatch()`, `buildFetchParams()`
  - `validateComps()`, `validateCompsWithMls()`, `deduplicateByMls()` for filtering
  - `computeDataRecencyDays()` — shared utility (extracted from predict.ts in KIN-14)
  - All 6 callers import from compService — no inline RPC calls remain
- **Unified Comp Pipeline (KIN-14)**: Diagnostics endpoint is single comp authority
  - `diagnostics.ts` fetches, validates, enriches, IQR-trims comps AND computes `marketPosition`
  - `predict.ts` is pure computation: `responseVersion: 3` with only `propertySituation`, `marginInputBase`, `spec`
  - Frontend sources comp data from `DiagnosticSummary` callback (not predict response)
  - `refreshNonce` pattern: WhatIfAnalysis increments nonce → DiagnosticTab watches and re-fetches
  - IQR exclusions use MLS numbers (stable identifiers) via `Set<string>`, not array indices
- Trigger.dev jobs import from `../../src/lib/` (see `summarize.ts` → `aiService`, `snapshot-comps.ts` → `compService`)
- DataGrid: Tailwind-native `src/components/ui/DataGrid.tsx` + `src/hooks/useDataGrid.ts` (replaced AG Grid)
  - `DataGridColumn<T>` typed interface: `render`, `format`, `getValue`, `headerRender`, `defaultSort`, `getRowClass`
  - `useSortedData()` hook, `filterData()` pure function
  - 9 consumers migrated: CommunitiesList, CommunityMarket, CommunityProperties, CommunityBacklog, CommunityLots, CommunityJobLots, PropertyComps, AllPropertiesTable
  - Garman row highlighting via `getRowClass` prop (not row-level CSS rules)
- **Shared UI Components** (added in UI audit cleanup):
  - `TabBar.tsx` — segment control tabs (bg-gray-100 pill style), used by CompetitiveLadder, RossCommunityDashboard, LegacyCommunityDashboard, CommunityLots
  - `Tooltip.tsx` — dark bg hover tooltip, used by WhatIfAnalysis (margin $) and CompetitiveLadder (similarity breakdown)
- **Design Token Standard**: Use `text-ink`, `text-ink-muted`, `text-brand`, `bg-brand`, `bg-surface` from global.css — never hardcode `#2C3E50`, `#5A6C7D`, `#FA4616`
- **Status Color Standard**: `green-50`/`green-700` for success, `amber-50`/`amber-600` for warnings — never `green-100` or `orange-100`
- **Badge Standard**: 2 variants — pill (`rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-xs`) and rectangular (`rounded px-2.5 py-1 text-sm font-semibold`)

## Component Relationships
- `WhatIfAnalysis.tsx` → state container, single scroll page (no tab toggle), diagnostic + scenarios sections
  - Decomposed into: `WhatIfOverviewCards.tsx` (banner, verdict, property card, skeleton), `WhatIfScenariosSection.tsx` (incentives, scenario table, positioning map), `WhatIfTypes.ts` (WhatIfResponse, LadderPool)
  - Old monolithic `WhatIfAnalysisView.tsx` deleted (PR #61)
- `DiagnosticTab.tsx` → `onDiagnosticLoaded` callback prop sends `DiagnosticSummary` to parent
- `DiagnosticSummaryStrip.tsx` → signals in collapsible accordion (all collapsed by default), drivers removed (KIN-18)
- `ChangeLog.tsx` → collapsed by default, summary line always visible, entries expand on click
- `MarketPositionResult` and `IQRDetails` types defined in `whatIfEngine.ts`
- Badge helpers (`statusBadgeClasses`, `matchBadgeClasses`, `matchLabel`) consolidated in `src/lib/compBadgeHelpers.ts`
- Shared diagnostic helpers (`DRIVER_TO_SIGNAL`, `getStatusClasses`, `findLinkedSignal`) in `src/lib/diagnosticHelpers.ts`
- `LotForm.tsx` — shared form extracted from AddLotForm/EditLotForm (PR #61)

## Key Constants
- **All-In Carry Cost (KIN-24)**: `LOAN_CARRY_ANNUAL_RATE`: 0.12, `OTHER_CARRY_PCT_ANNUAL_RATE`: 0.025, `OTHER_CARRY_FLAT_MONTHLY`: 850, `DAYS_PER_MONTH`: 30
  - `dailyCarryCost(listPrice)` — centralized helper in `whatIfEngine.ts`
  - Scenario table shows Loan Carry + Other Carry as separate columns
  - Overview/property card shows combined number with tooltip breakdown
  - SQL functions `compute_portfolio_performance()` and `community_metrics()` are price-aware; `overview_metrics()` dropped and unified into `compute_portfolio_performance()` (migration `20260207130000`)
  - Carry thresholds: green ≤$12K, yellow ≤$35K, red >$35K (community monthly level)
  - `p3Engine.ts` still on legacy `0.0002` rate (internal scoring, not user-facing)
- `IQR_MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE`: 10, `IQR_MIN_RETAINED`: 5, `IQR_K`: 2.0
- Similarity score thresholds: ≤0.15 Strong, ≤0.30 Good, >0.30 Fair
- Market position: >+5% overpriced, ±5% aligned, <-5% underpriced
- Score display: internal 10=best, display inverted via `displayScore()` so users see 0=best/10=worst
- Positioning map outlier threshold: 1.5× subject value (PPSF and DOM)

## Codex Review Learnings (Feb 2026)
- Dead code cleaned up in diagnostic-page-redesign: ~160 lines of orphaned market comp state/handlers removed from WhatIfAnalysis.tsx
- Middleware optimization: early-exit for public routes without refresh token is a good perf pattern
- `HttpError` class in predict.ts is a clean pattern for typed error handling in API routes
- DataGrid migration: Codex caught Garman row-highlight regression → added `getRowClass` prop
- ARIA: `aria-sort` belongs on `role="columnheader"` container, not on the `<button>` inside it
- PostHog tracking should be in `useEffect`, not render-time ref comparisons
- PR #61 tech debt: Codex decomposed WhatIfAnalysisView (702 lines) into 3 files; required adding `data-testid` attrs lost in decomposition
- PR #61 rebase: When rebasing large PRs after merging feature work, categorize conflicts into "structural only" (use --theirs) vs "business logic" (manual merge)
